video.agency.evidence: [影魔·codex] 图1第1行第1–7格（0–1.5秒），树人逼近时，我基本保持正面悬浮、双爪下垂，无法辨认主动观察或应对威胁的变化，有原地等待感。第2行第1–8格（2–3.75秒）可见我收紧下沉、火光渐暗，说明正在蓄力；但肩部出现亮点时，不能确认我有受击震动或转向攻击最凶者的反应。站在我的立场，蓄力意图可读，挨打时的即时应对拿不准，按要求判fail。；[树人·claude] 0–1.5 s (frames 0.000–1.500): the treants run in from all sides and close on him, which is fine. 1.75–5.75 s: they crowd round him, and sparks flash on his shoulder armour at 3.000, 3.500 and 3.750, so some hits do land. But from 4.000 to 5.750 the whole group dims into a dark mass, and I can't make out any of us swinging an arm, so I can't confirm the swing every ~0.7 s holds steady to the end. More importantly, the release and the deaths are out of cause and effect. The pillars only show up at 6.000 (the spec says 5.3 s), and by 6.250 they're already spread across the whole field, past the treants. Yet at 6.500 and 6.750 several treants near him are still standing upright among the pillars, still moving. At 7.000 some are still standing or only halfway down. Only around 7.250 are they all lying on the ground. That is 'treants keep walking among the pillars / treants fall only after a delay', when they should die and drop the instant the ring passes through them. From 9.250 to 11.750 there are small figures in the distant background that look like they're still standing or moving, and I can't tell if they're living treants. That's another uncertainty.

video.gaze.evidence: [影魔·codex] 图1第1行（0–1.75秒）看不清我是否扫视四周来敌；第2–3行（2–5.75秒）头脸细节小且逐渐变暗，无法确认我锁定最凶的攻击者、低吼时盯住正前方树人。第4行第1–3格（6–6.5秒）虽可见展开双臂，但不能确认仰脸后低头追看灵魂柱扫中的目标；第5行至第6行（8–11.75秒）也无法辨认低头扫视尸圈及最终注视前方尸体。不能把面朝画面前方直接认定为看镜头，但规定的视线对象与切换均缺乏清楚证据，按要求判fail。；[树人·claude] 0–1.5 s (frames 0.000–1.500): the treants' bodies all face him as they rush in, so their gaze roughly checks out. 1.75–5.75 s: the treants clustered round him are small, low-contrast silhouettes, and from 4.000 to 5.750 the whole group turns into a dark mass. I can't see any head angle or tilt, so I can't confirm they keep looking up at him while they strike. At 6.500–7.000, as the pillars sweep through, the treants still standing among them face ambiguous directions, and I can't tell if they're still looking at him. This can't be verified, so per the rule it's a fail.

video.readability.evidence: [audience·claude] Overall story I can get from the sheet: a fiery demon in the center (0.0–1.75s) is surrounded by a dark horde; the horde piles onto it (2.0–3.75s); dark spikes erupt from the ground (6.0–6.5s); the creatures are thrown back (6.5–7.25s); the demon is left standing alone among bodies on the ground (8.0–11.75s). But the key beats are unclear: (1) The cast itself is not readable. At 3.0–3.75s there are only a few small fire points and a dark gray ring. From 4.0–5.75s the demon is completely buried under the horde, and the red light fades until it is almost dark (5.0–5.75s). A first-time viewer is more likely to think the demon was overwhelmed or killed than that it is charging a skill. (2) The spikes appear abruptly at 6.0s and do not visibly come from the demon. They are dark gray against a gray sky with low contrast, so it is hard to tell who cast them. The effect is also not flashy. (3) In the result (9.0–11.75s), the pale white shapes on the ground look like ice, frost or debris as much as bodies, so it is not certain the horde was killed. The caster, the moment the skill fires and the outcome are all uncertain, so this fails.
